## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results yet. The starting architecture scored 0 on the same seed. In earlier searches a uniform 0 meant the world differed from its description, and only a mask-layout hedge ever escaped zero (world 2, about 0.22). Nothing is ruled out yet. Possible deviations include the action layout (transposed, flipped, type-minor order), where DONE sits, obs axes transposed or channel-last relative to the mask, and footprint or anchor offsets. This round follows the program. It runs the unchanged reference net, a 16-layout hedge (8 grid symmetries times type-major and type-minor order), a 5x5 head conv for footprint and anchor shifts, a hedge for DONE at index 0, and a hedge on obs symmetries plus a channel-last reading. A sixth candidate combines all of these so that any nonzero training success can be traced back. All candidates use the reference recipe, so differences come from the network's assumptions. With one seed, gaps under about 0.07 may be noise.

### Round 2
All six round-1 trials scored 0 on dev and in training. The ruled-out deviations, as sole causes and allowing for seed luck, are: the 16 grid-symmetry × type-major/minor action layouts, 8 obs symmetries, a channel-last obs, DONE at index 0, and footprint or anchor shifts within a 5x5 receptive field. Obs channel permutations never needed testing, because the dense 1x1 stem already absorbs any channel order. One case explains a uniform zero across all six trials: they share code that, if n_place != n_types*Y*X, falls back to a dense Linear remap. That kind of remap never escaped zero in earlier searches. This round, every candidate therefore infers structured layouts from n_place: K*H*W grids with H and W within ±2 of Y and X (any K, which covers per-layer actions), in major or minor order and transposed, plus valid-anchor-only layouts. Each candidate also carries one extra bet: more samples, scrambled obs pixels, global context with a wider head, depth with a longer horizon, or DONE placed first.

### Round 3
All 12 trials score 0 on dev and in training. Ruled out as the only deviation: the 16 action layouts (8 grid symmetries, type-major or type-minor order), DONE-first indexing, obs symmetries, a channel-last obs, a learned pixel remap of the obs, action counts other than T*Y*X, anchor offsets up to 2 cells (5x5 head), and global context. Gamma 0.97, a deeper trunk and 1 PPO epoch also scored 0. Every net so far shares one trunk: a 1x1 stem squeezes all 6 layers of every column into about 40 features before any spatial reasoning. A learned 1x1 stem does not care how the obs channels are ordered, so channel order cannot explain the zeros. More likely, a cross-layer computation is the bottleneck: where a brick lands, and whether every footprint cell at that layer is missing. Possibly this world is simply harder (larger or taller targets). This round changes that assumption with per-layer 2D processing (layers as batch, shared weights), footprint pooling and global attention. The hedges that cost little stay in.

### Round 4
All 18 trials scored 0 on both dev and training success. The tests rule out these deviations as the sole cause: the 16 grid symmetries in type-major and type-minor action order; DONE placed first; action grids near T*Y*X; obs flips, transposes and a channel-last reading; anchor or footprint offsets within 2 cells; a lack of global context; per-layer landing reasoning; footprint pooling; up to 425k samples; and a longer horizon. A learned 1x1 stem can absorb any permutation of obs channels, so channel order is unlikely to be the cause. Three explanations remain plausible. First, an arbitrary scramble of action indices, of obs cells, or of both, which no conv-aligned head can fix. Second, an obs or return scale that breaks optimisation: a large value loss would dominate the global gradient clip. Third, a world that cannot be solved. This last round bets on layout-free dense paths summed at full scale with default init (never zero-init), a fully flat MLP, and a scale-robust variant of the reference.
